reference: Documented private spool format, literal independent payload bytes, Bash decimal time/PID shape checks and independent stat/cmp observations. These are contract checks, not external batch parity; no consumer is started.
coverage: Bash reports batch as an enabled builtin.
Bash help exposes the documented stdin form, immediate scheduling description, and job ID format.
Private spool bytes, mode, unique IDs, empty/terminated input boundaries and argument/spool/stdin failures.
exclusions: Consumer execution, load scheduling and daemon integration require the future disposable VM or scheduler mock. Queue artifact tests do not execute jobs.

cases.purpose: Bash type metadata must identify batch as a builtin in the exact candidate. This checks availability without invoking the scheduler operation.
Bash help metadata must contain the documented stdin usage, immediate-as-low-load description, and job ID shape. The checks use only help and shell pattern matching; batch is not called.
cases.script:
doc=$(help batch)
[[ $doc == *'batch < script'* && $doc == *'currently immediate'* && $doc == *'Jobid format is <seconds-since-epoch>.<pid>.<seq>'* ]]
printf '%s\n' 'documented-interface-ok'

cases.purpose: Queue two inert private spool artifacts; verify bytes, appended LF, 0600 mode and unique documented IDs without starting a consumer.
cases.script:
export BASHCRON_SPOOL_DIR=spool
printf 'printf should-never-run > executed' > input
batch < input > first-message
batch < input > second-message
mapfile -t first < first-message
mapfile -t second < second-message
read -r word id1 scheduled forword time1 <<< "${first[0]}"
read -r word2 id2 scheduled2 forword2 time2 <<< "${second[0]}"
[[ $word == job && $word2 == job && $scheduled == scheduled && $forword == for ]]
[[ $scheduled2 == scheduled && $forword2 == for && $id1 != "$id2" ]]
[[ $id1 =~ ^[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]{6}$ && $id2 =~ ^[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]{6}$ ]]
[[ ${id1%%.*} == "$time1" && ${id2%%.*} == "$time2" ]]
for item in "$id1" "$id2"; do
 printf '# run_at=%s\nprintf should-never-run > executed\n' "${item%%.*}" > expected
 cmp "spool/atjobs/$item.job" expected
 [[ $(stat -c %a "spool/atjobs/$item.job") == 600 ]]
done
[[ ! -e executed ]]
printf 'private jobs preserved bytes, mode and unique IDs\n'
cases.stdout: private jobs preserved bytes, mode and unique IDs

cases.purpose: Reject operands, a regular-file spool parent and closed stdin; verify no partial job directory is created.
cases.script:
export BASHCRON_SPOOL_DIR=spool
if batch unexpected; then rc=0; else rc=$?; fi
printf 'argument=%s\n' "$rc"
[[ ! -e spool ]]
printf obstacle > blocked
export BASHCRON_SPOOL_DIR=blocked/sub
if batch <<< input; then rc=0; else rc=$?; fi
printf 'spool=%s\n' "$rc"
export BASHCRON_SPOOL_DIR=spool
if batch <&-; then rc=0; else rc=$?; fi
printf 'read=%s\n' "$rc"
[[ ! -e spool ]]

cases.purpose: Check that a separate cron consumer accepts queued jobs, executes them once in FIFO order, and applies the intended immediate/low-load policy.
cases.reason: The producer and consumer are each covered separately; an end-to-end batch -> cron run --once case with a fixed clock is implementable now.

cases.purpose: Empty stdin adds one script newline; terminated input retains exactly one terminator.
cases.script:
export BASHCRON_SPOOL_DIR=spool
: > empty
printf 'inert\n' > input
batch < empty > message
read -r word job rest < message
printf '# run_at=%s\n\n' "${job%%.*}" > expected
cmp "spool/atjobs/$job.job" expected
batch < input > message
read -r word job rest < message
printf '# run_at=%s\ninert\n' "${job%%.*}" > expected
cmp "spool/atjobs/$job.job" expected
printf 'newline boundaries verified\n'
